chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskhan, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'If it were not for what preceded me by the son of al-Khattab, no one would commit adultery except a wretched person.'

key_terms.بُنَيُّ الْخَطَّابِ: the son of al-Khattab (referring to Umar ibn al-Khattab)
key_terms.سَبَقَنِي إِلَيْهِ: preceded me to it / anticipated me in it

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the cause of widespread adultery in his time?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) observes that adultery had become so prevalent that it was no longer confined to the 'wretched' (shaqi), but had spread to the general populace. He attributes this moral decline to the influence or era of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that Umar's policies or example contributed to the normalization of this sin. This statement is found in the chapter on marriage laws in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the social context of early Islamic society.
